english: I give you my son as a pledge. He will live in your village. Then I give you the son of my brother. Will you guard him? I will guard him, and he will eat with my sons. When will the two sons return home? They will stay for three winters. Then they will return. If your people break the peace, your son will not return. My people will not break it. I swear it by Father Sky.

english: Brother, you have come back! For seven summers we did not see you. Sister, I have come. Do our father and mother live? They live. Our mother is old now, and she weeps for you. english: Uncle, let me fight the foes! I long for fame. Why do you desire war? The strangers did us no harm. The fameless man dies, and no one remembers him. Listen to me. He who builds peace wins imperishable fame. Is that true, uncle? It is true. We praise Of-True-Fame in song, who built the peace with the hill people. Then I will learn his songs.

english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep, our hearts pain us when we see this: a man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself. And the sheep has no wool."

english: Mistress, set me free! I long for my children. You are a captive. My husband bought you for ten cows. My kin will pay a ransom for me. My brother has much wealth. Then send word to him. If he pays, you will go free. Who will go to him? Our shepherd goes there in the spring. He will tell it to him. Where does he dwell?

english: My lord says: come to our feast with your men. What will there be at the feast? Mead, meat and songs. Will your old men drink with us, or your young men alone? All will come. Then we will come. We will lead a yearling calf as a gift for your lord. He will rejoice, and we will sing for you.

english: Why are you sad? Do you long for your village? I long for it. There the birds sing in the morning. Our birds sing too. Listen! I have heard them. But I do not know their song. When the barley ripens, you will return home. Then will you remember me? I will remember you, and you will come to us again.

english: Daughter, which path leads to the settlement of the chief? Who are you, and why do you seek him? My lord has sent me to him with words. Follow the path along the river. Go toward the dawn. When the sun is above you, you will see the fence of the settlement. You are kindly, daughter. May your herd grow! May you return home unharmed!
